/AWAR D 1. Vide this judgment/award, I shall dispose off the DAR bearing MACT no. 474/2024 filed by IO SI Bir Singh PS Raj Park, in regard to death of Sh. Lal Babu (in short, the deceased), who died in a road vehicular accident on 11.02.2024.
2. Brief facts as DAR are that on 11.02.2024 deceased, while driving his vehicle, bearing registration no. DL 4S DM 8776, was going to his work.

Therefore, R3 cannot be absolved from its liability on this ground.

As such R1 was charge-sheeted for offences under section 279/304A IPC.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether deceased Lal Babu, S/o Sh. Satya Narain Yadav expired due to injuries suffered in road traffic accident on 11.02.2024 at about 10:00 am, at Sultan Mazara,
near PNB Bank, Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing no. UP 23 AT 2972 which was being driven by driver Furkan S/o Sh. Iliyas on the said date, time and place?
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
My issue wise findings in the case are as under :-
ISSUE NO.1 1. Whether deceased Lal Babu, S/o Sh. Satya Narain Yadav expired due to injuries suffered in road traffic accident on 11.02.2024 at about 10:00 am, at Sultan Mazara,
near PNB Bank, Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle bearing no. UP 23 AT 2972 which was being driven by driver Furkan S/o Sh. Iliyas on the said date, time and place?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
Now, the question which arises for determination is as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden MACT Case No. 474/2024/2024 (FIR no.
151/24) Ritu Devi & Ors.. Vs. Frukan & Ors.
VIKRAM 2026.04.01 of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs.
Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

However,
for want of bed in Agarsain Hosptial when they were shifting the deceased to BSA Hospital,
condition of deceased become worse.
If an injured person dies while being shifted to another hospital for better treatment, the original injury caused by the accident is generally considered the proximate cause of death.
As per MLC of deceased, deceased was having abrasion on right foot and right lower leg, abrasion on left foot and pain in right hip.
Therefore, R3 cannot be absolved from its liability on this ground.
Therefore, the petitioners have become entitled to be compensated for death of deceased in the above accident, but computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
Basically only three facts need to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death : (a) age of the deceased; (b) income of the deceased; and the (c) the number of dependents.
The issues to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of dependency are (i)
additions/deductions to be made for arriving at the income;
(ii) the deduction to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased; and (iii) the multiplier to be applied with reference of the age of the deceased.
In this regard, though not quoted, reliance is placed upon, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.
(2009) 6 SCC 121.
22.
Therefore, the monthly income of deceased is arrived as per minimum wages of a matriculate person prevalent in Delhi during the period in question.
25. Considering the fact that deceased was aged about 43 years at the time of accident, future prospects @ 25 % has to be awarded in favour of petitioners in view of recent pronouncement made by Constitutional Bench of Apex Court in the case titled as National Insurance Company Ltd. v.
Pranay Sethi & Ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680, as well as in view of recent decision of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in appeal Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pooja & Ors, in MAC APP No.
798/2011.
26.
Thus, there has to be deduction of "one forth(1/4th)", as per the mandate of Sarla Verma (supra).
The offending vehicle was insured with R3 at the time of accident.
It is claim of R3 that the owner of offending vehicle had expired on 27.07.2022 and despite that policy was renewed and obtaioned in the name of R1/registered owner of the offending vehicle by playing fraud and misrepresentation and thus the policy was void ab initio.
